Lingaraj Temple

India > Odisha > Bhubaneswar

Architectural Splendour of Somavamsi Kings

The majestic Lingaraj Temple stands as the crowning jewel of temple architecture in Bhubaneswar. Built during the 11th century CE by the Somavamsi dynasty rulers, this grand 55-meter tall spire dominates the historic skyline of the Old Town.

The sanctum represents the Harihara form, a syncretic manifestation uniting Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu. The sprawling temple complex comprises over 150 subsidiary shrines enclosed within massive laterite stone boundary walls.

Constructed from red sandstone in classical Rekha Deula and Pidha Deula styles, the temple walls feature intricate stone carvings portraying celestial nymphs, mythological episodes, and floral motifs.

Visiting Timings

Opening time - 06:00 AM Closing time - 09:00 PM

Celebrations & Festivals

The grand celebration of Mahashivaratri attracts tens of thousands of devotees who observe day-long fasts until the sacred Mahadipa is hoisted atop the temple spire. Another major event is Ashokashtami (the annual Car Festival of Lord Lingaraj), celebrated with immense cultural fervour.

Connectivity & How to Reach

Nearest Airport : Biju Patnaik International Airport (BBI), approximately 4 km away.

Nearest Railway Station : Bhubaneswar Railway Station (BBS), approximately 5.5 km away.
